understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to solve each KA59 level by moving and/or switching between selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked '+' in the semantic grid is occupied by a selectable piece at the same time, which triggers WIN for the level and ultimately completes the full set of levels.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN to shift the currently selected piece by one 3-pixel cell per action (x increases right, y increases down). Walls (#) and boundaries could block movement, and some adjacent objects could potentially be pushed if they were pushable and directly in the movement direction, moving along with the selected piece; however, the 'movement_*_blocked' indicators were only hints and did not guarantee failure or success. When multiple selectables existed, control could be switched by CLICKing the exact pixel/grid coordinate of another selectable listed in the objects/state (same coordinate system as player.position), after which movement commands applied to the newly selected piece.

understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to solve each KA59 level by moving and/or switching between selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked '+' in the semantic grid is occupied by a selectable piece at the same time, which triggers WIN for the level and ultimately completes the full set of levels.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN to shift the currently selected piece by one 3-pixel cell per action (x increases right, y increases down). Walls (#) and boundaries could block movement, and some adjacent objects could potentially be pushed if they were pushable and directly in the movement direction, moving along with the selected piece; however, the 'movement_*_blocked' indicators were only hints and did not guarantee failure or success. When multiple selectables existed, control could be switched by CLICKing the exact pixel/grid coordinate of another selectable listed in the objects/state (same coordinate system as player.position), after which movement commands applied to the newly selected piece.
